issues.competing_evidence: Barrett+20 Table 2 visibly prints d=8 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax is 6.06324±0.08540 mas and Bailer-Jones+21 geometric posterior is 163.925 pc (p16/p84=161.624/166.157); ReimersHagen+00 gives ~190 pc from an M3.5 donor template; Vogel+11 abstract gives 140±50 pc.
issues.why_it_matters: The 8 pc entry is physically inconsistent with parallax and alters absolute and radio luminosity estimates by orders of magnitude.
issues.needed_action: Seek source-author/data-table clarification about the printed 8 pc value and its input; retain the exact published discrepancy and adopt the exact-source Gaia posterior unless a documented correction is found.

issues.parameter: subclass / detached versus episodic mass transfer
issues.competing_evidence: ReimersHagen+00 and Vogel+11 call the source a low-accretion polar/pre-polar; TovmassianZharikov+07 establishes synchronism and reports tentative stream evidence near L1; Parsons+21 finds M-dwarf RLFF=0.95±0.03 under a thermal-equilibrium radius model and notes possible episodic RLO, but their 2017 spectra show no stream and cover <half an orbit. SIMBAD otype RS* conflicts with the primary literature.
issues.why_it_matters: The catalog label changes whether HS 0922 is treated as detached/pre-polar or as a mass-transferring polar and affects evolutionary interpretation.
issues.needed_action: Keep the secure synchronized magnetic-polar classification, but decide whether the public subtype should read “LARP/pre-polar candidate” or “polar with possible episodic Roche-lobe overflow”; no single scenario is selected from present evidence.

issues.parameter: TESS flare decay and physical origin
issues.competing_evidence: Wang+24 Table 2 excerpt reports decay 1031 s, while its text gives ~1002 s and a ~8 min rise; it describes the event near orbital phase 0.82 as possibly on the far donor hemisphere. Bruch+25 indexed excerpt reports two short bursts with different characteristics and says one was previously noticed by Wang+24. The publisher full texts were not retrievable in this session.
issues.why_it_matters: Separating a donor-star flare from an accretion burst affects its relevance to transient emission and the meaning of flare energetics.
issues.needed_action: Inspect Wang+24 Sect. 3.1.3/Table 2 and Bruch+25 Sect. 3.3.44/its tables in original full text; resolve the 1002/1031 s wording and decide whether either event is securely an accretion burst.
